request.state: The user has changed the scheduling constraint: more than five parallel Muse worktrees are allowed because they expect the standard library to be the largest effort. That expectation is a planning hypothesis, not measured effort. Existing product: AI-authored SaaS, Rust CLI scaffold and TextMate editor only, 39 Can drafts and 21 handwritten JS targets, TS stdlib, JS/workerd execution, shared auth/operations/DAISYUI-HTMX/MCP, no duplicate compiler or business-authority engine. Each HUMAN-launched Muse lead creates one worktree, delegates disjoint files inside it, and repeats focused PR/review/test/merge cycles. No further sessions are launched by Codex. Reuse Cloudflare services, runtime APIs and maintained SDKs; no full custom platform reimplementation. Preserve exact scalars, one authoritative commit path, current grants, scoped receipts, file provenance and deterministic inline BDD. D1 fenced batches and DO-local transactions are distinct supported owners, never cross-service atomicity. New population/history/AI proposals need explicit contracts, not invented implementations. Target similarly substantial owned backlogs, fewer shared-file conflicts, and an early real integrated app. Hardware disk/load is constrained; neither parallel throughput nor exact work estimates are measured. Option A has seven lanes: 1 Rust compiler/checker/codegen plus lint/format/LSP/editor; 2 pure values/types/schema/codec stdlib; 3 data/query/CRUD/permissions/fenced commits/migrations/replay; 4 durable events/timers/outbox/delivery plus providers and file lifecycle; 5 UI/components/i18n; 6 identity/HTTP/MCP adapters; 7 platform assembly/build/local dev/deploy/BDD/integration/releases. A separates stdlib domains and keeps fewer cross-lane effect interfaces, but lane4 owns both durable machinery and provider breadth. Option B has eight lanes: the same seven ownership groups, except lane4 is durable work only and a new lane owns provider adapters plus files. B lets external adapters progress independently and removes breadth from work scheduling, but adds a work/provider/file contract, another checkout/build load and another lead; provider semantics still need early ownership interfaces. Both keep query authorization with lane3, UI rendering with lane5-equivalent, auth state changes through the kernel, a single named writer per shared manifest/contract, and a typed producer-first bootstrap followed by real integration. No option can claim completion using mocks or merely passing syntax.

partition.instructions: Which starting partition better fits the revised freedom to split library work, considering workload breadth, integration interfaces and resource overhead with unmeasured speed?

criteria.A: A: Seven owners; durable execution, providers and files share one lane.
criteria.B: B: Eight owners; separate the durable engine from provider/file adapters.
